units: SI unless stated; energies in eV or kg (E / c^2)

mmp_max_signal_energy.source: Maldacena, Milekhin & Popov, arXiv:1807.04726: (2.3), (5.31); section 5.4: a signal above the throat binding energy makes a near-extremal black hole
mmp_max_signal_energy.formula: E_max ~ |E_min| = G_N q^2/(256 r_e^3) with r_e^2 = pi q^2 l_p^2/g^2, so E_max r_e/(hbar c) = g^2/(256 pi) [der]
mmp_max_signal_energy.assumptions: U(1) coupling g = 0.30 (electromagnetic) or 0.36 (hypercharge near the weak scale) [assumption]; MMP give the threshold only to order of magnitude
mmp_max_signal_energy.reading: one signal may carry about 1e-4 of the energy of a single quantum whose wavelength is the mouth radius r_e

mmp_standard_model_size.source: arXiv:1807.04726 section 8: with Standard Model fields the distance d between the mouths must be below the electroweak scale (say 1/TeV), r_e much smaller
mmp_standard_model_size.formula: d_max = hbar c / (1 TeV) [der: unit conversion]
mmp_standard_model_size.reading: with Standard Model matter alone the wormhole is sub-attometre; larger ones need new massless charged fields

mm_humanly_traversable.source: Maldacena & Milekhin, arXiv:2008.06618: formulas after (3.26), numbers (3.27), orbit condition (B.32) d > 0.5 ly, information <= ~c2 quanta per l (section 2)
mm_humanly_traversable.assumptions: a Randall-Sundrum II dark sector with a gauged dark U(1) (the authors call it science fiction); no formation mechanism; mouths kept apart by orbiting

casimir_static_throats.source: Garattini, arXiv:1907.03623: (29), (41)-(42), footnote 6 (omega = 3 gives r0 = 1.0166 l_P); Hochberg, Popov & Sushkov, gr-qc/9701064: numerical throat r(0) = 0.02 l_P and an analytic example r(0) = 67 l_P from their Eq. (8)
casimir_static_throats.reading: the static Casimir- or vacuum-polarisation-supported throats in these papers are Planck scale; neither paper treats dynamics or a signal
